author: cskiraly
content:
As you say, Waggle is a base protocol. It can be a good fit for almost everything because it is a common base abstraction layer. It is a naming convention, and the conceptual model behind that naming convention, mostly. Even that is still to be tested because it still misses a refined specification, but that's AFAIK on the way, and that's a good thing. What it does not define is the use case specific protocol logic sitting on top. That's actually part of the waggle thesis: it does not want to specify that.  

To illustrate it better also to those less into networking stacks, here are some analogies that I hope will make this clear:
- "we agreed to use UDP, why are we speaking of Waggle. "
- "we agreed to use IP, why are we discussing UDP"
- " we agreed to use ....
Once upon a time, There was no IP and TCP defined separately. It was one mess of a protocol. Then people realised it helps to separate those two, and they stand on their own. That doesn't make IP solve all our networking needs.

Similarly, Waggle has its stated goals of being that base layer. The agreement you mention was on trying to have this common base vocabulary and layer defined and used. I don't think we can see more into it. In fact this was explicitly discussed in that specific meeting. 

Yet, as uncomfortable as it is, interoperable networking protocols are slightly more complex than just a base layer, or saying that we have topics that have names and pieces that we exchange. Seacast is an attempt to map out and solve that complexity. The part waggle does not try to solve.

author: barnabasbusa
content:
hey all, quick update on the pq p2p work, and sorry for the naming mixup earlier. we've ended up with two separate test networks and they can't talk to each other, so it's worth knowing which one you're building for.

**pq-devnet-0-seacast** runs cskiraly's SEACAST (<https://github.com/cskiraly/seacast-spec>) over plain **gossipsub** for now, not waggle. the spec also defines waggle and raw quic bindings, but only the gossipsub one is implemented today: payloads and aggregates go out as erasure-coded segments on their own gossip topic. prysm (<https://github.com/cskiraly/prysm/tree/seacast-devnet-clean>) and silver (<https://github.com/gattaca-com/pq-silver/tree/seacast-gossip>) already have it, though silver's aggregate signature check is stubbed for now so don't copy that part. you can spin it up with:
`kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package@pq --args-file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package/pq/.github/tests/pq-devnet-0-seacast.yaml --image-download always`

**pq-devnet-0-waggle** is Waggle (<https://github.com/libp2p/specs/pull/732>) with Kamil's fast proof broadcast (<https://notes.ethereum.org/@kamilsa/rk_I4TMJme>), where the aggregate proof gets chunked and the VC signs a header committing to the chunks, so that one needs VC changes as well. lighthouse has it on <https://github.com/kamilsa/lighthouse/tree/leanvm-proof-broadcast>, and you can run it with:
`kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package@pq --args-file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package/pq/.github/tests/pq-devnet-0-waggle.yaml --image-download always`

author: barnabasbusa
content:
if you're working on either, let us know which one and push it to a `pq-devnet-0-seacast` or `pq-devnet-0-waggle` branch, then we'll add it to the image builder so you get `ethpandaops/<client>:<tag>` images automatically. please test interop locally against the reference clients before asking for a devnet. it would also really help if you could expose aggregation and proof timings in a common way (aggregate built, chunks received, proof reassembled, verified), so we can pull them into xatu/dora and actually compare seacast, waggle and plain gossipsub on real numbers.

once a couple of clients interop on either network we'll put up a public devnet and do proper measurements at scale.
